youtube_items.title: [YT] How false news can spread - Noah Tavlin
youtube_items.summary:
There's a quote usually attributed
to the writer Mark Twain that goes, "A lie can travel 
halfway around the world while the truth is putting on its shoes." Funny thing about that. There's reason to doubt
that Mark Twain ever said this at all, thus, ironically, proving the point. And today, the quote, whoever said it,
is truer than ever before. In previous decades, 
most media with global reach consisted of several 
major newspapers and networks which had the resources
to gather information directly. Outlets like Reuters
and the Associated Press that aggregate or rereport stories
were relatively rare compared to today. The speed with which 
information spreads now has created the ideal conditions for
a phenomenon known as circular reporting. This is when publication A
publishes misinformat

youtube_items.title: [YT] How dangerous are TikTok & Co. for democracy?
youtube_items.summary:
Is social media a
threat to democracy? Online radicalization is
dividing societies globally. Many people blame social media:
we interact in echo chambers and algorithms make sure we see
opinions similar to our own. What's behind this? Let's take a closer look- on SHIFT. Messaging friends, checking out new
dances, and sneaking a peek at your crush's posts...all while
catching up on the latest news. That’s how a lot people use
TikTok, Instagram, or Facebook. But that’s just one side of
social media, says Indian software developer Sairaj Balaji. People need to understand that social
media now is not the same as it was ten years ago. It is now a word minefield, a
battlefield for information warfare. Information warfare using
AI, but we'll get to that later. Everyone is fighting for your
attent

youtube_items.title: [YT] Maria Ressa - Disinformation on Social Media Is Threat to Democracy
youtube_items.summary:
American biologist, E.O.
Wilson said it best. We're facing paleolithic
emotions, medieval institutions, and God-like technology. Social media has become a
behavior modification system and we are Pavlov's dogs, experimented on in real time
with disastrous consequences. Facebook is the world's
largest distributor of news and yet studies have shown that lies laced with anger and hate spread faster and further
than really boring facts. The very platforms and social media that deliver the facts to
you are biased against facts. They're biased against journalists. They are by design dividing
us and radicalizing us.

analysis.problem: The spread of false information and disinformation on social media platforms, such as TikTok and Facebook, threatens democracy and divides societies globally
analysis.root_cause: The combination of paleolithic emotions, medieval institutions, and God-like technology, as well as the use of algorithms that prioritize sensational and provocative content, creates an environment where lies and misinformation can spread quickly
leverage_points: Social media companies and their algorithms

proposed_actions.action: Implementing fact-checking mechanisms and labeling suspicious content on social media platforms
proposed_actions.measurable_goal: Reduce the spread of false information by 20% within the next 6 months

proposed_actions.action: Developing and implementing media literacy programs in schools and communities
proposed_actions.measurable_goal: Increase the number of people who can critically evaluate online information by 30% within the next year

evidence: A lie can travel halfway around the world while the truth is putting on its shoes, as quoted by Mark Twain
Studies have shown that lies laced with anger and hate spread faster on social media platforms, as mentioned by Maria Ressa
analysis.generalization: This problem connects to the domains of human (culture and social media), civilization (democracy and institutions), and planet (global interconnectedness and technology)
analysis.summary: The spread of false information on social media threatens democracy and requires immediate attention and action from social media companies, governments, and individuals
